newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- outperforms Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- outperforms Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds outperformed the sliding Treasury market Wednesday, falling only slightly as the government long bond lost nearly a point.
Muni traders said some bonds were off as much as 5/8, but the overall market was down only about 1/4.
Treasury bonds, in contrast, suffered big losses after a disappointing auction of 10-year notes. The government long bond was down 30/32 at 95-23/32 to yield 6.97 percent.
The day's new muni issues were priced very aggressively, according to a market analyst. But traders said demand has been steady nonetheless.
Analysts pointed in particular, to Tennessee's $173 million general obligation competitive issue, won by J.P. Morgan Securities Inc.
J.P. Morgan reoffered the 2017 bonds at a 5.45 percent yield, and said later in the day it had only a $30 million balance.

The day's largest new issue came from Bear Stearns & Co., which priced and then repriced Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority's deal. At the repricing, the firm increased the deal to $566 million from $469 million and raised yields in some maturities.
Orange County, Fla., sold $351 million certificates of participation through PaineWebber Inc., which restructured the issue but left yields unchanged.
In the muni secondary market, Dade County, Fla., water and sewer FGIC 5-1/4s of 2026 were bid at 5.74 percent, up four basis points from Tuesday and two basis points above midday quotes.
Upper Occoquan Sewer Authority Va., MBIA 5.0s of 2025 were up two basis points to 5.78 percent, after being quoted down two earlier in the day.
In debt futures, June municipal bond futures lost 15/32 to 114-26/32, while June Treasury bonds dropped 25/32 to 109-10/32. The MOB spread widened to 176 ticks from 166 at the close Tuesday.
Thursday's supply is expected to total $340 million in 19 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $220 million in five sales, with a $125 million Massachusetts Ports deal through Merrill Lynch & Co. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 14 sales totaling $120 million are on the schedule. A $54 million Minnesota Health Facilities Authority deal at 1030 EDT is the largest.
